text: One blustery October morning, a heavily armed merchant brig from Liverpool ignored the warning flags hoisted at Barra Point.
Relying on favorable winds and a low tide, its captain fired a mock salute and steered directly past the sandbar without paying the mandated bars of iron and sacks of salt.
When royal harbor runners paddled out to demand compliance, the British captain laughed from the quarterdeck: 'The river is free to the Crown; we pay no tribute to local sovereigns!'
He ordered all sails unfurled and vanished upriver toward the trading factories.
